premise.title: The Last Relay Above Aster
premise.logline: A junior orbital relay technician must choose which emergency message to forward with only enough battery for one verified transmission.
premise.immediate_objective: choose and justify one reliable rescue transmission under a strict battery limit
premise.inciting_event: A damaged communications buoy emits a distress packet apparently dated six minutes in the future.
premise.central_problem: Is the timing discrepancy clock drift or a real fault in the relay network?
premise.wonder_or_discovery: A damaged communications buoy emits a distress packet apparently dated six minutes in the future.
premise.stakes: A mistaken transmission could divert rescue vessels; waiting could strand a crew.
constraints: A six-minute timestamp anomaly does not establish time travel.
Power reserve, signal delay and battery drain must remain consistent.
The technician cannot instantaneously communicate across light-minutes.
An unread packet cannot be used as known evidence.
premise.meaningful_choice_pressure: The protagonist must choose either forward_verified_payload or attempt_second_measurement before the evidence window closes.
premise.mystery_or_forward_question: Is the timing discrepancy clock drift or a real fault in the relay network?
premise.local_payoff: Resolve exactly what can be reported from existing observations; leave cause, hidden motives and unverified future outcomes open.
persistent_outcomes_possible: An evidence-bounded report may be recorded only if produced and witnessed in the actual story.
Professional trust may shift only if the story earns that relationship change.
A future follow-up may become eligible but must not be treated as already authorized.
world_specific_elements: battery-powered emergency radios, orbital telemetry, delayed long-range transmissions
none; no teleportation or verified time travel
A technician can forward an independently checked distress packet.
A false distress relay diverts limited rescue resources.
